title: C Programming Foundations
subtitle: Build the C memory model needed for real data structures.
description: A cumulative introduction to C execution, control flow, functions, arrays, pointers, structs, dynamic memory, multi-file design, and deterministic testing.
prerequisites: Basic comfort using a browser-based editor.
intendedFor: Learners following the cumulative C data-structures and algorithms pathway.
learningGoals: Trace C execution and memory state.
Write safe multi-file C11 programs.
Use pointers, structs, and dynamic memory with explicit ownership.
Build and test a cumulative record-management project.

courseOverview.recommendedSequence: Follow modules in order. Each standard module extends the same cumulative workspace and ends with a module project. The final module is one cumulative capstone topic.
courseOverview.summary: A cumulative introduction to C execution, control flow, functions, arrays, pointers, structs, dynamic memory, multi-file design, and deterministic testing.

moduleSummary.title: How C Programs Execute
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Understand the shape of a C program and the path from source text to a running executable.
moduleSummary.outputFocus: Create the initial campus-ops program and a deterministic diagnostic harness.

moduleSummary.title: Decisions and Loops
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Trace control flow before writing branches and loops that terminate correctly.
moduleSummary.outputFocus: Extend campus-ops with a menu loop and command dispatcher.

moduleSummary.title: Functions and Program Decomposition
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Break a program into testable functions while understanding parameters, scope, and call-stack behavior.
moduleSummary.outputFocus: Refactor campus-ops around reusable service functions.

moduleSummary.title: Arrays and Strings
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Use contiguous storage safely for records, text, searching, insertion, and removal.

moduleSummary.title: Pointers and Memory Addresses
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Use pointers to observe and update memory without losing ownership or dereferencing invalid addresses.
moduleSummary.outputFocus: Add pointer-based update helpers and trace tests.

moduleSummary.title: Structs and Self-Referential Types
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Model records and nodes with structs while making representation invariants explicit.
moduleSummary.outputFocus: Add request records and linked history node types.

moduleSummary.title: Dynamic Memory and Ownership
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Allocate, resize, transfer, and release heap memory with explicit ownership rules.
moduleSummary.outputFocus: Convert the service registry into a dynamic store.

moduleSummary.title: Multi-File C Programs and Testing
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Separate public interfaces, private implementation, builds, and deterministic tests.
moduleSummary.outputFocus: Prepare the reusable foundation library used by later courses.

moduleSummary.title: C Foundations Capstone
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Combine control flow, functions, arrays, pointers, structs, dynamic memory, and multi-file organization.
moduleSummary.outputFocus: Build a dynamic multi-file student record manager with safe strings, validated commands, search, update, deletion, tests, and complete cleanup.

authoringGuidance: This course must always use subjectSlug c, courseSlug c-programming-foundations, profileId c, and the shared C multi-file workspace policy.
Teach the idea in language-neutral pseudocode before showing the complete C implementation.
Use pseudocode_input for algorithm completion, reorder, trace, or full-write activities; never validate raw prose by exact string matching.
Validate pseudocode through normalized structure rules and deterministic trace scenarios. AI may explain failures but is not the primary pass/fail checker.
Every pointer-heavy, recursive, tree, heap, sorting, or graph operation begins with a manual algorithm_animation using stable layouts and one state change per frame.
Place a predict-next-step interaction before important animation transitions.
Every C code_input uses fixedLanguage c, recipeType fixed_tests, entryFilePath main.c, and complete starterFiles and solutionFiles.
Keep learner TODOs in named implementation .c files and preserve supplied headers and deterministic main.c harnesses.
Compile all authored .c files as C11 and free official-solution allocations before exit.
Complexity is graded with counts, choices, traces, or structured pseudocode—not exact Big-O prose.
Every standard module ends with one progressive module project; the final module contains exactly one cumulative capstone topic.

animationRules: Use previous, next, play or pause, replay, and a visible step counter.
Keep layouts stable; animate links, active cells, call frames, or edges rather than moving the whole structure.
Synchronize heap tree and array states, recursion and call stack states, and graph state with queue or stack state.
Prefer five to ten meaningful frames and one state transition per frame.
pseudocodeRules: Use dialect zoeskoul-v1 and inputKind pseudocode_input.
Accept equivalent variable names and harmless syntax variants after normalization.
Require explicit termination, state updates, and invariant-preserving branches.
Use structure plus scenario execution for pass/fail.
Keep the learner pseudocode visible beside the following C translation exercise.
workspaceRules: Reuse the same course workspace across module projects.
Do not ask learners to create boilerplate files or remember compiler commands.
Each new module adds focused .h/.c files while preserving prior passing tests.
Project steps are progressive and may not reset earlier work.

assessmentAndDelivery.recommendedRhythm: Two or three traced lessons plus one hands-on implementation session each week.
assessmentAndDelivery.closingNote: Learners complete C Programming Foundations with an executable cumulative project and an analysis record.

disallowedConcepts: linked lists as a finished abstraction
